newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Woodside seeks trunkline environmental ok.
newsitem.headline: Woodside seeks trunkline environmental ok.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd, operator of the North West Shelf gas project off the coast of Western Australia, said on Friday it had sought environmental approval for its plan to build a second trunkline linking the offshore gas production facilities to shore.
Woodside said the application has been submitted to the Commonwealth and Western Australian governments.
The existing 134 kilometre subsea trunkline was approaching capacity with existing sales commitments.
A second trunkline would be needed for additional domestic gas volumes in the short term and to cater for future expansion of LNG production.
The North-West Shelf joint venturers last October unveiled a $6.0 billion expansion of the project.
Woodside said the joint venturers were expected to commit to the second offshore trunkline when sufficient new market opportunites were confirmed.
Preliminary design engineering was under way and a commission date of 2000 had been proposed.
Woodside said last December it had awarded the design and management contract for the second trunkline to a joint venture between Brown & Root Engineering Pty ltd and JP Kenny Pty Ltd.
The equal stakeholders in the North West Shelf gas project are Woodside, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd British Petroleum Plc, Chevron Corp Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Japan Australia LNG (MIMI) Pty Ltd.
